chunks: Ibn Nuh said: I heard a group of our companions in Egypt mentioned that Abu Sahl al-Nuubakhti was asked how this position reached Shaykh Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh and not him.

He said: They are more knowledgeable about who they have chosen. I am a man who meets the adversaries and debates with them. If I knew his place as Abul Qasim did, and the proof was pressed upon me regarding his place, perhaps I would indicate his place. But as for Abul Qasim, even if the Divine Proof were under his cloak and cut with scissors, he would not remove his cloak, or he said something like this.

key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The Divine Proof (referring to the Imam)
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ رُوحٍ: Al-Husayn ibn Ruh (the fourth deputy of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Why was Husayn ibn Ruh chosen as the Imam over Abu Sahl al-Nuubakhti?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the distinction between scholarly debate and the innate, divinely ordained status of the Imam during the Minor Occultation. Abu Sahl al-Nuubakhti illustrates that while he possessed the ability to argue and identify the Imam, al-Husayn ibn Ruh’s selection was due to a deeper, intrinsic connection to the Divine Proof (al-Hujjah), symbolized by the metaphor of the cloak that remains undisturbed even under pressure. This underscores the Shia belief in the infallible selection of representatives who embody the Imam's presence with unique spiritual authority.
